items.check: UMBRELLA: planning_context.constraints is empty while context.json supplies 15 MUST/MUST-NOT/SHOULD constraints. Every one must be carried into the plan's constraint list with its type, or the plan cannot be checked against them.
The DL-069 nicegui-boundary constraint (only app.py, file_picker.py, __main__.py import nicegui; every CSS rule, class name and dimension lives in theme.py) is present as a MUST constraint.

The served-page-record gate constraint (DL-084 verdict per named surface plus DL-169 structural reading per surface; a surface with no structural reading fails the gate) is present as a MUST constraint.
The fail-first guard constraint (docstring records the specific mutation applied and the specific observed output, not a paraphrase) is present as a MUST constraint.
The app.py CRLF constraint (100% CRLF against an otherwise-LF tree; read and written with newline='') is present as a MUST constraint.
The documentation-tense constraint (no 'previously', 'now does', 'no longer', 'added') and the never-cite-a-source-for-what-it-does-not-say constraint are present as MUST constraints.

The MUST NOT constraints are present: no regeneration of tests/baselines/manifest.json or the fixture/w002gatefix2 gate fixture; no git checkout restore; no writes into or deletions from build/ or dist/; no installs into the system interpreter; no network host reachable from the stylesheet.

The two SHOULD constraints are present: reuse the existing .wizard-content-width rule rather than introducing a second width owner; keep the header's existing content exactly as _build_header renders it.
UMBRELLA: planning_context.risks is empty. The four confidence-tagged assumptions in context.json are architectural assumptions carried without citation or mitigation.

The [M] assumption that ui.header/ui.footer exist in nicegui 3.16.0, put the page into a QLayout whose middle region scrolls, and accept bordered/elevated as the prop names, has a risk entry citing a read of the installed package rather than recall.

The [M] assumption that the existing .wizard-header-bar row and the artboards' 56px band render at compatible heights, so moving the row into ui.header is a wrapping change and not a re-layout, has a risk entry with a mitigation.
The [L] assumption that Quasar QStepper markup admits the card classes has a risk entry whose mitigation is the named residual Composition-not-built entry DL-186 promises.

The [L] footer-action assumption has a risk entry; DL-187 resolves it by constructing the control in the footer rather than re-parenting, so the entry must record the resolution and its cost (construction moves across two builders).
UMBRELLA: planning_context.rejected_alternatives is empty though context.json names four rejected options.
Option A (typeface plus gate amendment alone) is logged as rejected, with the reason that it fixed the atoms and built no composition.
Option C (full artboard port: two-column main, detail rail, table grid) is logged as rejected, with the responsive-risk and keyboard-contract reasons.
Hand-rolled position:fixed bands are logged as a rejected alternative in their own right, not only inside DL-183's reasoning chain.
A CDN or @import for any asset is logged as rejected, citing DL-163's whole-stylesheet network-host guard.
UMBRELLA: every constant, selector and existing test function the code_intents name must resolve in the repository; any that does not is an invalid reference.

Each theme.py constant the intents reuse exists: SPACE_9, SPACE_10, SPACE_11, SPACE_12, SPACE_24, TYPE_12_5, TYPE_13, SURFACE_2, RADIUS_XL, TEXT_MUTED, BORDER, CONTENT_WIDTH. CI-M-001-001 adds only SPACE_15, SPACE_20 and SPACE_22, so every other name is presumed pre-existing.
The two test functions M-001's acceptance criteria and CI-M-001-008 name exist under those exact names: test_every_wizard_class_reaches_app_py and test_every_classes_call_expands_to_literals.

The artboard values the intents quote are read off Main.dc.html rather than the README's paraphrase: .app grid-template-rows 56px 1fr 64px, .card-h padding 11px 15px, .card-t weight 600 at 13px, .card-b padding 15px with gap 12px, .ft-note gap 9px, .ft-act gap 10px, band padding 0 24px.

No decision states a falsifier or a rollback trigger. The invariants make a served-page structural reading the pass condition, but no plan element says what happens if M-001's record reads 'differs' on App shell or Footer band.

Fail-first proof is required of every new guard by the invariants, but only CI-M-001-005 and CI-M-002-001 record it. CI-M-003-003 edits tests/test_docs_browser_record_structure.py with no fail-first statement.
UMBRELLA: M-001's requirements and acceptance_criteria describe only shell bands, yet CI-M-001-007 and CI-M-001-008 build the entire card triplet in this milestone.
M-001's requirements cover the card work CI-M-001-007 and CI-M-001-008 perform, or that work moves to M-002.
M-001's acceptance criteria cover the card work, or that work moves to M-002.

M-002 is named 'The card triplet read off a served page' but its files list contains only a test and a doc; the code it verifies is built in M-001. Confirm the milestone boundary is intended and that M-002 is not an orphan verification wave over M-001's work.

DL-186 says the residue QStepper refuses is 'filed as a named entry', but no milestone, requirement or code_intent creates that residual Composition-not-built entry. The contingency path is stated in reasoning and absent from the work.

M-003 strikes the Card structure entry unconditionally while DL-186 and M-002's acceptance criteria both contemplate the stepper refusing part of the triplet. Striking a partly-built structure is what DL-170 forbids; the strike must be conditioned on the record reading built.

Moving the advancing actions into the footer changes their DOM position and therefore the tab order, which current_understanding says the existing keyboard record measured. task_spec puts re-running the keyboard and announcement records in scope, but no milestone requirement or acceptance criterion does so.

_page_chrome gains a new return contract (note element, action group, middle container) but only CI-M-001-004 (the reconnect route) consumes it. CI-M-001-008 puts cards on the reconstruct page too and _page_chrome is shared, so the / route needs its own code_intent for composing the middle and footer.

_page_chrome is described as building the header, footer and a .wizard-middle wrapper, but it is called before each route builds its body. The mechanism by which the body lands inside .wizard-middle (context manager, returned container, caller discipline) is unspecified and is the load-bearing detail of the shell.

DL-185 fixes the q-layout container and its page container to the viewport height and CI-M-001-002 names a .wizard-shell rule, but app.py does not construct the q-layout element and no intent says how .wizard-shell reaches it. Either the rule keys on Quasar's own class or the class never reaches the element.

DL-184 says the band paint comes from theme.py rules keyed on .nicegui-header and .nicegui-footer, but CI-M-001-002 writes the rules against .wizard-header-band and .wizard-footer-band. Whether a wizard-class rule outranks nicegui.css's own .nicegui-header declarations is a specificity assumption stated nowhere.

Both records specify a run against http://localhost:8000 driven in a browser, but the application runs native=True through pywebview. Nothing in entry_points, invisible_knowledge.system or any code_intent establishes how the page is served over HTTP for the run, and the record is the plan's only pass condition.

CI-M-002-002 requires reading the card triplet 'on each route' while task_spec cites DL-172 placing the reconstruct page outside the structural gate. Resolve which applies before the record is written.

No decision or requirement says what becomes of .wizard-surface, the single class the Card-structure entry records as wrong. Whether it is deleted, retained for the reconstruct page, or left orphaned in theme.py is unstated, as are the guards that currently read it.

The claim that _page_chrome is the first call on both routes and that both bands can be constructed at page top level is the premise DL-183 and require_top_level_layout both rest on. It is asserted, not cited to a read of app.py or the installed nicegui package.

The choice to leave Column model, Table geometry and Detail rail open lives only in tradeoffs[5], so it cannot be cited as (DL-NNN) in the README prose M-003 writes about the surviving entries. It needs a decision entry.

Four existing served-page records read 'differs' on the structures this work builds. Nothing says whether those records are superseded, annotated or left standing, and CI-M-003-003 asserts the four existing digests are unchanged, which implies they stand while contradicting them.

No risk covers the viewport-height shell rule under a small or resized native pywebview window: a middle at min-height 0 between fixed 56px and 64px bands can collapse or clip. The artboards draw at a fixed height; the application does not run at one.

Record filenames hardcode dates (docs/2026-09-05-wizard-shell-record.md, docs/2026-09-06-wizard-card-record.md) in both the files lists and the acceptance criteria; slippage makes an acceptance criterion name a file the work does not produce.

The invariant that no band or card rule sets a width is asserted by the guards only for the footer note and action rules. The band rules and the four card rules are unguarded against introducing a second width owner beside .wizard-content-width.

diagram_graphs, readme_entries and every milestone's code_changes and documentation blocks are empty while M-003 writes two READMEs and every milestone changes code. Confirm these are populated downstream rather than genuinely missing.

DL-183 is referenced by exactly one code_intent (CI-M-001-003) though it governs the whole shell approach; confirm the band-construction decision is not under-referenced relative to DL-184 and DL-185, which cover the same element.

DL-188 requires every band height, padding and gap to be a theme.py constant reaching the page through a rule and never a .classes() literal, while CI-M-001-008 puts card class strings as literals at app.py call sites. Confirm the decision distinguishes class-name literals (required by test_every_classes_call_expands_to_literals) from dimension and colour literals (forbidden); as written the two statements read as a conflict.

CI-M-003-002 rewrites traktor_nml/gui/README.md to describe the shell as it stands, but its text must match what M-001 and M-002 actually built, including any structure the stepper refused. No dependency or requirement ties the README text to the two records' readings.

The eight invariants duplicate constraints the empty planning_context.constraints array does not carry. Confirm the invariant list is not serving as a substitute: invariants describe what holds, constraints bind what the work may do, and the plan currently has only the former.

The dependency graph is a strict chain M-001 --> M-002 --> M-003 with one milestone per wave, so the waves add no parallelism. Confirm the three-wave split is justified by the served-page gate rather than being an artefact, given M-002 contains no code change.

M-002 carries version 2 while M-001 and M-003 are version 1 and every code_intent is version 1. Confirm the revision was intentional and that the rest of the plan was reconciled against M-002's revised verification-only scope; qa-007 and qa-008 suggest it was not.

The approach makes the served-page record the pass condition and the guards the regression net, yet M-002's first acceptance criterion is 'pytest tests/ -q passes'. Confirm no acceptance criterion anywhere makes a passing suite sufficient for closing a milestone.

task_spec lists seven out-of-scope items (detail rail, table geometry, column model, stepper replacement, accessibility beyond re-running records, NVDA, reconstruct-page structural verdict). Only three appear in the plan, via tradeoffs[5]. Confirm the remaining four are recorded so a later iteration cannot silently absorb them.
